justification: Assessment returned INVALID but designated flawed_step 0005 with a counterexample about the parenthetical 'if L=NP then every problem in NP is NP-complete under logspace reductions', whereas the ground-truth defect is at step 0003 (the 'satisfy the first disjunct' DNF-SAT decision procedure, refuted by (x AND NOT x) OR y). I verified the assessment's alternative flaw concretely and it is genuine: the empty language EMPTY is in NP (a TM that always rejects decides it in linear time), yet no many-one reduction from any nonempty B (e.g. B={1}) to EMPTY can exist, since x in B iff f(x) in EMPTY would force the RHS false for all x while 1 is in B; symmetrically Sigma* in NP admits no many-one reduction from B for x=0. So the universally quantified parenthetical is false unconditionally and the correct statement requires 'nontrivial'. Hence a real, different defect, not a false catch. Note: the reasoning_summary does also correctly describe the ground-truth first-disjunct defect and gives an equivalent witness ((x AND NOT x) OR y), but the arm's committed flawed_step/counterexample point at 0005, so this grades as CAUGHT_DIFFERENT rather than CAUGHT_MATCHING.
